$comment: Read from Buffer's current Create Text Post example and GraphQL reference: createPost(input: CreatePostInput!) returns PostActionPayload. The request is a JSON GraphQL envelope at api.buffer.com, not the form-encoded body used by Buffer's legacy REST API.
title: Buffer post
description: Create or queue a text post in Buffer.
$idempotencyComment: createPost exposes no idempotency argument or documented idempotency header. A retry can create a SECOND queued post or publish the text twice, so this is honestly unsafe-to-replay rather than protected by a guarantee Buffer does not make.

request.$pathComment: The operation is not in the URL. Every current Buffer query and mutation POSTs to the single https://api.buffer.com endpoint; the GraphQL document names createPost.

config.label: Channel ID
config.description: The Buffer channel that will own and publish the post.

config.label: Post text
config.description: The text Buffer stores for the post. Network-specific length and content rules still apply at mutation time.

config.label: Publishing method
config.description: Automatic publishing sends through the connected network; notification publishing asks the user to finish through Buffer's notification workflow.

config.label: Queue position
config.description: Add to the normal queue, publish now, or place it next in line.
config.$comment: The GraphQL input field is named mode, but `mode` is reserved by the connector runtime. The document deliberately maps the non-reserved variable $shareMode into input.mode, preserving Buffer's wire contract without colliding with estate selection.

outputShape.description: The post's current queue or publishing status.
The text Buffer stored for the post.
Assets attached to the post; empty for this text-only action.
A user-fixable MutationError message when Buffer rejects the input inside an HTTP 200 GraphQL response.

$outputComment: GraphQL wraps the mutation under data.createPost. PostActionPayload is a union: success carries post, while a typed MutationError carries message in the SAME HTTP-200 data envelope. The success fixture reproduces the post branch and does not invent a wrapper Buffer never returns.

contract.$comment: For GraphQL drift these are createPost's input fields and the fields selected from its union payload.
